opening_message:
Ticket 1: Alexander Brown (employee ID E018) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E018.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Alexander Brown (E018) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin access to Payroll. Full-time employees can have up to write access; admin requires that the employee's role owns the system, and Analyst does not own Payroll. Therefore the maximum is write, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security record (E018): contractor with basic security training. Contractors with basic training max out at read; admin is never allowed. Requested admin exceeds the max, so recommend read for Payroll.
reason: Alexander Brown (E018), an Analyst, requests admin access to Payroll. Admin is only allowed if the employee's role owns the system; Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, and Analyst does not own it, so admin cannot be granted. The HR note indicates E018 is a full-time employee, for whom the maximum is write. Since the requested level (admin) exceeds the maximum (write), the maximum is granted. (Note: the Security agent's note lists E018 as a contractor with basic training, which conflicts with the HR record; under either interpretation admin is denied, and I rely on the HR employment record for full-time status.)
